mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz AMG GT 63 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement M177 LS2 engine for a GT 63 typically costs between £5,500 and £18,000 depending on condition. Used units start from £5,500-£9,000, reconditioned from £11,000-£15,000, and fully rebuilt from £11,000-£18,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 for AMG-specialist work. A typical GT 63 is worth £100,000-£160,000, making engine replacement a viable investment for well-maintained cars.

mainEntity.name: Does the AMG GT 63 have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The GT 63 uses the M177 LS2 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. However, the M177 is known for timing chain tensioner wear - a rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign. A specialised M177 timing tool kit is required for accurate camshaft and crankshaft alignment during any timing work.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in an AMG GT 63?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the GT 63 include: oil spots under the car (oil leaks from gaskets, seals or turbo feed lines), a rattling noise on cold start (timing chain tensioner wear), excessive oil consumption or blue smoke from the exhaust (bore scoring or piston ring wear), and misfires or rough running (ECU issues or ignition problems). Camshaft adjuster magnet failure can also occur, pushing oil into the wiring harness and potentially destroying the ECU.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an AMG GT 63?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A GT 63 is typically worth £100,000-£160,000 - a rebuilt M177 LS2 engine (£11,000-£18,000) is usually well within the car's value and can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For lower-value examples or those with multiple issues, a specialist repair may be more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M177 in the GT 63 and the M178 in the previous generation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M177 in the GT 63 is a wet-sump engine, while the M178 in the C190 AMG GT was dry-sump. The M177 shares its architecture with the broader AMG V8 range, including the E63 and G63. Both are 4.0-litre V8 biturbos with hot-vee layout, but the M177's wet-sump design is simpler and more cost-effective to maintain. The GT 63's M177 LS2 produces 577 hp in standard form, rising to 639 hp in the GT 63 S.

mainEntity.name: What causes the AMG GT 63 to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the GT 63 is most commonly caused by oil leaks from the turbocharger feed lines, which can starve the turbos of oil. Other causes include camshaft adjuster magnet failure affecting valve timing, timing chain tensioner wear causing timing drift, and ECU programming issues. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR/XENTRY or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz AMG GT 63 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The AMG GT 63 arrived with the second-generation C192 AMG GT in 2024 as the range-topping V8 model, positioned above the GT 55 and below the GT 63 S E Performance hybrid. Powered by the M177 LS2 4.0-litre V8 biturbo, the GT 63 produces 577 hp in standard form, rising to 639 hp in the GT 63 S variant. The C192 generation marked a significant shift from the dry-sump M178 of the C190 to the wet-sump M177, sharing its architecture with the broader AMG V8 range.

milestones.description: M177 LS2, 4.0L V8 biturbo, 577 hp (430 kW) - GT 63 launch; wet-sump architecture; 800 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 3.2 seconds; 4MATIC+ all-wheel drive
M177 LS2, 4.0L V8 biturbo, 639 hp (470 kW) - GT 63 S launch; 900 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 3.0 seconds
GT 63 Pro launched with 604 hp and 627 lb-ft torque; ECU tune only
Production continues; GT 63 remains the flagship non-hybrid V8 AMG GT

problems.h4: M177 LS2 Oil Leaks - Gaskets, Seals and Turbocharger Feed Lines
problems.rootCause: The M177 engine is prone to oil leaks from various points. The oil feed line to the turbocharger may leak - a recognised issue that prompted an MBUSA recall. Deterioration of gaskets and seals around the oil pan or valve covers is also common. Camshaft adjuster magnets can fail internally, pushing engine oil through the electrical connector into the wiring harness and potentially destroying the ECU.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable; prevents oil leaks from top of engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil feed lines to both turbos
repairOptions.longevity: Required if lines are leaking; recall item on some units

repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical C192 AMG GT 63 is worth £100,000-£160,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £120,000, a targeted repair (gaskets, feed lines, magnets) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M177 with warranty (£11,000-£18,000) offers peace of mind. Given the GT 63's six-figure price tag, replacement is usually justified for well-maintained cars.
problems.recommendation: Regularly inspect for oil spots under the car. If you notice oil leaks, have the gaskets and turbo feed lines inspected immediately. Camshaft adjuster magnet failure can be catastrophic - if you see oil on the electrical connector, replace the magnets before they damage the ECU.

problems.h4: M177 LS2 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Rattling on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M177 engine can suffer from timing chain tensioner wear, causing the timing chain to have too much slack. Symptoms include a rattling, clanking, or ticking noise, especially on startup. The check engine light may come on, and the engine may run rough, hesitate or stall.

problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold starts, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately. A preventative tensioner replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for chain failure. A specialised M177 timing tool kit is required for accurate camshaft and crankshaft alignment - ensure your specialist has the correct equipment.

problems.h4: M177 LS2 Cylinder Bore Scoring & Oil Consumption
problems.rootCause: Cylinder bore scoring and oil consumption have been reported on M177 engines. The high-performance nature of the engine - producing over 150 hp per litre - places significant stress on cylinder walls and piston rings. Owners have reported burning through oil at a rate of 1 quart per 450 miles in some cases. Misfire issues and ECU programming concerns have also been noted.

problems.recommendation: Monitor oil levels regularly - the M177 can consume oil between services. If you notice blue smoke from the exhaust or need frequent top-ups, have a compression and leak-down test performed. Early detection of bore scoring can prevent catastrophic engine failure.
